title: The lot-reach measurements: how far a lot reaches from each street line and from its corner point, from the recorded outline - measurements only, no law (work order Part 0, first new file; gaps K1, K4, K12; D-090 R227, R229, R238)
objective: Add the lot-reach measurements the work order's Part 0 needs (docs/plans/R6B_RESULTS_CONNECTION_WORK_ORDER_2026-10-06.md, section 8 'Part 0', the new file services/api/app/spatial/lot_reach.py and its test; section 5 gaps K1, K4 and K12). A pure, deterministic module that takes what the existing single-lot site geometry already derives (services/api/app/spatial/site_geometry: the prepared outline in EPSG:2263 feet, the confirmed street frontages and the relation between two frontage streets) and measures: (1) for each confirmed street frontage, the farthest perpendicular distance of any point of the outline from that frontage's street line; (2) where exactly two confirmed frontage streets meet as a corner: the angle between the two street lines, the corner point where their lines intersect, and the farthest straight-line distance of any point of the outline from that corner point. Each measurement is a labelled value in the package's own way (approximate, from the tax-map outline, with its basis in plain words); where it cannot be stated (no outline, a refused outline, an uncertain frontage, a frontage that is not straight, no corner relation) the value is unknown with the reason, never a zero and never a default. The module states measurements only: it applies no law, holds no 100-foot or 135-degree threshold, decides no coverage and no rear yard, and is called by nothing yet. No existing file changes.
business_reason: Gaps K1, K4 and K12 of the work order: the corner provisions reach only part of some corner lots, and today the engine takes one typed yes/no for the whole lot. The reach must be computed from the recorded outline and street lines and never typed by a user or a test. The owner's rules: no coverage of 100 percent for a whole lot until the geometry supports it (R238); a value the program does not have is shown as not known (R229); each important number has a test whose expected value comes independently of the program (R227). Independent expected values exist: the corner-reach reference case (the real lot and three made-up lots), reviewed and merged.
